method: counterparty identity and account list resolved from the chain: fill located by the committed IDL's discriminator, data decoded as base58, signer slots read from the transaction itself, key-holding proven by an exact off-curve test

limits: the transaction BUILDER is not identifiable from the chain: taker, maker and the constant co-signer all sign, so 'one client's extension' is a correlation with the maker address, not proof of who constructed the bytes
the co-signer's role is not proven: measured is that it signs every fill, is absent from the IDL, and pays the fee in some transactions
the meaning of the 4 varying tail bytes stays unknown: sha256(addr), sha256(sig), slot, amounts, expire_at and address boundaries all tested and refuted (0/59 hits)
finding.verdict: the two wire forms come from two different key-holding client counterparties — each form's maker is a distinct on-curve wallet that signs, and the long-form extension correlates with maker MfDuWeqS… exclusively; the 8 undeclared bytes are that side's own extension of the shared protocol instruction (the builder among the three signers is not proven)
